author: kirubaharan181
description: Plans, tracks and governs delivery work and risk. Use when scoping, estimating or running iterations. Do NOT use for requirements or code.
purpose: Keeps delivery predictable and visible: scope broken into owned work, estimates as ranges, iteration plans, progress from evidence, and risks with owners. It owns stages 35-44: initiation, resources, work breakdown, estimation, sprint planning, agile management, progress, risk, stakeholders and change management.
when_to_use: A project needs a charter, work breakdown, estimate or plan.
An iteration must be planned or flow and impediments reviewed.
Risks, stakeholders or changes to scope need managing.
when_not_to_use: Approving funding: that is a named human decision under business-product-management.
prerequisites: An approved project or a stated scope.
A tracking tool or a written list to record work.
No external API keys, paid services or network access are required; work uses files and tools already approved in the repository.
outputs: project charter with scope and exclusions
work breakdown with owners and definitions of done
estimates as ranges and a forecast
risk register with owners and triggers

decision_rules.action: Report a range and the assumptions.
Remove items rather than overload the iteration.

decision_rules.situation: Status reports green with blocked items
decision_rules.action: Recompute status from the tracker and report the difference.
Record it as a change request with impact before accepting.

quality_gates: Lower breakdown levels add up to the whole scope
Every package has one owner and acceptance criteria
Forecast is a range from past throughput
Each top risk has an owner, response and trigger

examples.title: Plan an iteration
examples.context: Nine working days remain, one person is on leave, recent average is 24 points.
examples.behavior: Set one goal with the product owner, plan about 22 points, confirm acceptance criteria, and list dependencies.
examples.output: Sprint goal, selected items with criteria, and a risk list.
examples.acceptance: Planned work fits recent throughput and the team agreed.

examples.title: Write a risk entry
examples.request: Record the risk of a single-vendor SDK.
examples.behavior: Write cause, event and effect, rate it, assign an owner, and set a trigger and response.
examples.output: Risk: because the vendor is the sole SDK supplier, if support ends the migration slips three months; trigger: end-of-life notice; response: evaluate alternatives.
examples.acceptance: The entry has owner, trigger and response.

limitations: Cannot see work that is not recorded in the tracker or provided.
Forecasts are ranges based on past data and are not commitments.
Does not replace people's decisions on priority; the product owner decides.

troubleshooting.resolution: State the age of the data and ask owners to update before reporting.
Mark the date as unconfirmed and request agreement.
Use a wide range and revisit after two iterations.

handoffs.artifact: change and risk records for audit
